Subject: Recap: Dedicated capacity discovery — Cyclone.ai (qualification & next steps)

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today — good discussion. I wanted to capture what we heard on the call and propose concrete next steps so we have alignment going into technical follow-ups. Please reply with any corrections.

Quick high-level recap
- Primary pain: highly variable inference costs + unpredictable latency during peak batch jobs. Nightly batch spikes and business-critical low-latency inference for product features.
- Current stack: Kubernetes-based microservices, in-house feature store on-prem, model hosting currently through a mix of vendor-managed endpoints and lightweight on-prem inference.
- Required isolation & compliance: data residency in US, VPC/network isolation preferred, SOC2 evidence requested.

Success criteria (what would make a Dedicated fit)
- Predictable sustained throughput: baseline 300–400 TPS (sustained)
- Peak handling: burst to ~1000–1300 TPS for 15–30 minutes, typically 2–4 times per day
- Latency target: P95 end-to-end for 512-token requests < 250ms
- Security: VPC isolation, customer-managed KMS for keys, audit logs retained for 90 days

Autoscale / burst expectations we heard
- Baseline pool should cover 300 TPS continuously
- Burst policy must support short 10–30min surges to ~1.1k TPS without manual intervention
- Tolerance for slightly higher latency during bursts if throughput preserved (prefer graceful degradation)

Attachments
- Attached: Cyclone_traffic_sample.csv (sample request traces), Cyclone_initial_MAP_v1.pdf (high level timeline & goals)

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Elena/Mark: confirm baseline vs peak numbers above and add any missing models or request patterns (e.g., long-context vs short).
2) Share a 48–72 hour traffic sample (CSV or logs) if possible — helps us size a Dedicated pool and recommend quantization/replicas.
3) We propose a two-part follow-up: a technical deep-dive with our infra SE (30–45m) and a commercial sketch (pricing ranges + MAP) the following week. Please propose 2 windows.
4) We will surface SOC2 evidence and a draft MAP by EOW.

Proposed timeline
- Technical deep-dive: next week
- PoC (if agreed): 2–4 week validation with telemetry and perf targets

I’ve CC'd Dev (SE) who will propose a specific Dedicated configuration after we receive the traffic sample.

Thanks —

Thanks Rishi — that summary looks right and is helpful. Couple of clarifications from our side:
- Baseline is closer to 300 TPS sustained (we've historically seen 250–350 depending on batch windows).
- Peak observed is ~1,000 TPS (rarely up to 1.3k) and bursts usually last ~20 minutes.
- Model mix: two production models — a quantized Llama2-70B derivative for higher-quality responses and a smaller distilled model for quick lookups. We may route ~65% of traffic to the small model during extreme bursts.
- Data residency: US-east required for primary region; would like hot-standby in US-west.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II report would be required as part of procurement.

I've attached a 48-hour sample export (attached). Also uploaded to the shared drive link you suggested.

Timeline: target decision by end of Q2; we’re trying to get budgets and security review lined up.

Happy to take the technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed afternoon PST — Mark and I are flexible.

— Elena

Great notes — I pulled a quick sketch on sizing after a first pass over the sample. High level observations and initial recommendations (will validate after full traffic matrix):

Observations- Traffic shows short high-volume spikes (~18–25 minutes) and a steady baseline of ~300 TPS. Many requests are short-context (<=128 tokens) but the Llama2-70B requests drive most compute during business hours.

Initial config suggestion (to meet your P95 <250ms for 512-token requests)
- Primary pool: Dedicated reserve of 6 H100-class GPUs in US-east with model-sharded serving for the Llama2-70B derivative.
- Secondary pool: 2–3 H100s in US-west (hot-standby) for regional failover and DR.
- Autoscaling: keep baseline capacity steady (no batching for low-latency paths), allow burst capacity via short-lived burst nodes — Redwood Dedicated supports automated burst policies (warm standby + prewarmed VMs) to handle the 10–30m surges.

Operational notes
- KV/prefix caching: we can reduce overall token compute for repeat requests which helps cost during sustained periods.
- Quantization: we recommend an int8 profile for the Llama2-70B derivative in Dedicated to reduce memory and increase throughput. We'll run a quick eval to validate quality.

What we need next from Cyclone to firm this up
1) Full 7-day traffic matrix by request type (short/long context split, tokens per request).
2) A prioritized list of models to include in the PoC and any strict isolation rules per model.
3) Compliance contacts to route SOC2/DPA requests.

I'll prepare a lightweight perf estimate and cost band (range) once we have the 7-day sample. Happy to take the deep-dive Tue/Wed — propose Tue 11:00–11:45 PST.

— Dev Patel
